rows.en:
What's more, the figure reflected in the crystal ball in front of her was herself, wearing a black robe.
That fortune-teller's robe...
What kind of trick is this?
Have I been deceived?{p}

"Well, you sure can't give a straight answer, can you?
I can't ask someone like you for anything.
I'm going home."
Fed up with Hirai, who had gone silent, the old woman marched right out of the tent.
As she left, the old woman glanced back at Hirai for just an instant.
With the light behind her, Hirai couldn't see her well, but those eyes and that smirking grin reminded her of someone.
"Wait!"{p}

She hurried after her, but outside the tent, there was no longer any sign of the old woman, she said.
With nothing else to do, Hirai went back into the tent, and found a letter tucked into the stand of the crystal ball on the table.{p}

The letter had been written by that fortune-teller, addressed to Hirai.
And it said...
Thank you, young lady.
Just as you wished, the curse has been fulfilled.
The other woman is no longer of this world.
Your lover whose heart strayed will come back to you, too.
However, that will happen only after you have finished the job.
Thank you. Thanks to you, I was able to finish my job.
I kept working as a fortune-teller for a very long time, but today, at last, I have been set free.
The keywords for release are the three listed below.
One: I want to curse someone.
Two: I'm prepared.
Three: I'm not scared.
When a client speaks these three phrases, you will be released from the job.
Small changes in the wording at the end do not matter.
You, too, please work hard at the job so that you can see your lover.
Well then, farewell.
...That's what it said, apparently.{p}

From the very next day, Hirai stopped coming to school and spent every day in the tent telling fortunes, I heard.
But you know, she really didn't have any special sixth sense after all.
So even though she called it fortune-telling, she just read out of books and stuff, and she could only give vague answers.
Do you think customers would come to a fortune-teller like that?
I think anyone would hate that.
You could trust a fortune you told yourself way more.
Once not a single customer came anymore, Hirai got more and more desperate.
She didn't even go home; she stayed in the tent telling fortunes all the time.
Her parents and the teachers went to the tent over and over, angry, trying to drag her back, but Hirai thought they were just customers, so neither side was getting through to the other, apparently.
And in the end, she got put in a hospital.
They said if it was somewhere close by, she might run away, so they put her in a hospital really far away, I heard.
It seems she couldn't even recognize Tanaka anymore, even though she'd loved him so much.
After all, the two of them aren't supposed to meet again until her job is done.
Hey, {a}.
Do you think what that fortune-teller wrote in the letter was the truth?{p}What do you think?
The letter told the truth
It was a nasty prank

I think so too.
Games like this used to be popular, right?
Like chain letters, or those curse letters...
"Anyone who hears this story............"
The ones that end like that.
Hirai's story feels like an elaborate prank to me, too.
She seems to have poured a lot of money into fortune-telling, after all.
Maybe it's closer to fraud than a prank.
Not that anyone knows what really happened, though.
After this incident, Tanaka went and married a gorgeous woman named Miwako, but once Hirai's job is finished, will he come back to her, even if it means leaving his wife?
Part of me kind of wants to see that, though...{p}

Oh, I know☆
{a}, you should go and be one of Hirai's customers.
My big sister knows which hospital Hirai's in, so it's no problem.
Okay, sometime... let's see, let's go together over summer vacation or something.
If you think of it as helping someone, you won't be scared.
Oh, right.
You think it's nothing but a nasty prank, don't you, {a}?
Then you won't be scared at all, will you?
It's decided. It's a promise.
Want to pinky swear?
Hee hee hee.
Well, that's the end of my story.
The seventh one never showed up after all.
What are you going to do?{p}

So it really is like that, huh.
If that letter was telling the truth, then where did the fortune-teller go once she was released from the job?
I think that old woman is suspicious.
If it's just like the letter says, the fortune-teller must be pretty old.
You can hide your face and body to some extent with makeup and a robe, and places like that keep the lights low, don't they?
You can fake your age pretty easily, you know.
Or maybe you don't age while you're living as a fortune-teller?
Come to think of it, Hirai looks young, you know.
Last holiday, I went with my big sister to visit her in the hospital.
That was the first time I'd ever met Hirai, but according to my sister, she hasn't changed one bit since back then.
She's the same age as my sister, so, um, she should be twenty-three this year, but however you look at her, she looks fifteen or sixteen.
And it's not like she's just trying to look young or anything.
The firmness and texture of her skin are completely different.
So the idea that time stops while you're living as a fortune-teller somehow doesn't seem so wrong to me.
I think lots of people still wish they could never age and never die, but do you think it's really such a good thing?
I mean, what did that letter say?
"Thank you," that's what.
If that fortune-teller had also taken over from some other fortune-teller somewhere, then they all want to be released, even if they have to find someone to take their place.
Then again, once death starts slowly creeping up on them, I bet they start saying
"I want to go back to never aging and never dying"
all over again.
Well, people always want what they can't have.
But if Hirai has turned into an old woman by the time she's released from the job, what will she do?
Will she marry Tanaka after he's turned into an old man?
I mean, sure, her wish would come true that way.
Whether she'd be happy or not is another matter.
It'd be lucky for her if she got released from the job soon, though.
Hmm, if I ever have someone I want to curse, maybe I'll go see her.
Since Hirai's fortunes never come true, the curse would probably be just for show, though...
I recommend her to anyone interested in never aging and never dying.
Okay, that's the end of my story.
But still, the seventh person isn't coming, are they?
I wonder if something happened...{p}

With that, the fortune-teller took the knife out of Hirai's hand.
"And I had prepared a very special ritual just for you!"
"I'm sorry.
I'm really sorry."
Hirai apologized desperately.
But she was never forgiven.
The ritual couldn't be stopped.
"It's too late.
You should not have hesitated.
Right now, this knife needs your hatred.
Your negative feelings toward the other woman...
Positive and negative. Yin and yang.
My sorcery lays a curse by sealing the power of two opposite poles into a single object.
The positive that answers your negative... in other words, the love for the other woman, has already been sealed into this knife."
At the fortune-teller's words, Hirai gasped.
Love... it can't be☆{p}

"Surely you understand by now.
That's right.
This knife has drunk Tanaka's blood.
With your hatred, a mere two or three drops would have fulfilled the curse, but his love wasn't nearly that deep, so I took the liberty of using all the blood in his body."
"That's horrible.
How horrible! How could you kill Tanaka?!"
"What are you saying?
Isn't this all exactly what you wished for?
The only request I accepted was to curse Tanaka's new girlfriend, after all."
The fortune-teller declared it flatly, without the faintest smile.
Hirai sank to her knees right where she stood.
She no longer had any idea what it was she had even wanted.{p}

"Oh dear, I'm not finished talking yet.
The trouble is, this knife is terribly angry.
To soothe its anger, I simply must have your blood.
I do ask for your understanding on that point.
Yes, I did say two or three drops earlier, but circumstances have changed, so there has been a change on my end as well."{p}

And then the fortune-teller raised the knife high over her head...
"I will be using all the blood in your body."{p}
The last thing Hirai's eyes saw was the knife swinging down, and the fortune-teller's grinning face...{p}

Hey, {a}.
Do you think a knife can really get angry?
Even if the fortune-teller says so, if nobody else can tell, there's no way to check, right?
What if it was all lies and nonsense...
This fortune-teller, you know, got arrested for fraud after this incident.
The bodies of young women kept turning up behind the tent, one after another.
Sadly, Hirai was one of them.
For some reason, every one of them had been drained of all the blood in her body, and no one could find even a trace of where all that blood had gone.
I wonder what the fortune-teller was planning to do with that blood.
Oh, right, about Tanaka: he hadn't been killed.
Far from being killed, he didn't have a single scratch on him.
I heard he's getting married soon.
See? After hearing a story like this, you can't just believe in fortune-telling so easily anymore, right?
If you're someone who's happier believing, I won't say anything, though.
Okay, that's the end of my story.
What should we do?
The seventh one still isn't here.{p}

I'll call it off.
I can't do something that terrifying after all.
Hirai had become completely terrified.
But what if that fortune-teller gets angry and puts a curse on me...?
When she thought about that, both choices scared her, and she didn't know what to do.{p}What on earth should I do...?
Go to the fortune-teller
Too scared after all; don't go

Hirai made up her mind.
She would absolutely not go.
And she decided to stop visiting that fortune-teller for good.
She was breaking her promise, after all, so there was no way she could go back, right?{p}

But you know, one day, all of a sudden, Tanaka became kind to her again, just like before.
Hirai had no idea what had happened, but she said she was happy all the same.
It was just as if a curse had been lifted.
That's what she said, apparently...{p}

Hey, {a}.
I wonder who that curse had been put on.
With a wicked witch's curse, sometimes it's put on the princess, and sometimes on the prince, right?
The first wicked witch that comes to mind is the fortune-teller, but after what happened, Hirai never went back, so she says she doesn't know what became of her.
My big sister tried going to the place Hirai told her about, but there was no tent or anything there.
There were still traces of where the tent had stood, though, so she figured it had been taken down and moved somewhere else.
The woman who'd been Tanaka's girlfriend stopped showing up too, just like that.
The strange thing is, Tanaka couldn't remember her name or where she lived at all.
He'd even been to her house, but he didn't know where it was, and they'd talked on the phone every night, but he didn't know her number...
Maybe she had some connection with the fortune-teller too.
In stories, the rule is that when the wicked witch dies, the curse is broken, but in real life, that'd be hard to confirm.{p}

Hee hee hee, {a}.
You get it now, right?
If Hirai had kept on going to that fortune-teller, she might have been eaten up by the wicked witch.
Fortune-telling isn't something you should get too wrapped up in.
Okay, that's the end of my story.
The seventh one isn't coming, so what are you going to do, {a}...?{p}

I'll go.
In the end, breaking her promise scared her more.{p}

Oh, so looks come second.
So it's not like faces don't matter to you at all, then.
Hmm.
So housework in general comes dead last, huh.
I see.
Well, that's a pretty common answer.
...Actually, about Hirai from before.
I told you she had really high ideals, right?
Hirai's ideal, you see, was...{p}

Someone like her big brother.
That brother of hers was supposed to be really cool.
Dependable, I guess you'd say. He was student council president and stuff.
He was smart, and he had a great personality too.
If he had any flaw, it was that he was soft on his little sister.
That's the kind of person he was.
You can see why Hirai would get so attached to her brother, right?
He was the brother she was proud of.
And Hirai was really beautiful, but...
her personality had a bit of a problem.{p}

She really did have great looks.
She was beautiful, and she had a great figure.
Guys were hitting on her all the time.
She often got scouted to be a model and stuff, too.
But her personality...
It seems she wasn't a really bad person or anything, though.
...She was a huge liar.
Hirai was hooked on fortune-telling, you see.
And she was always going around telling everyone the results.{p}

If a fortune said she'd get a boyfriend, she'd say she was going to introduce him to everyone soon.
If it said her money luck was good, she'd say she'd treat everyone sometime, and then she'd just forget.
She was a girl with a bit of a problem.
The reason she said stuff like that was that she truly believed the results of her fortunes, though.
To everyone else, she was just a liar.{p}

But don't you wonder why Hirai believed in fortunes that never came true?
According to her, as long as a fortune came true once in a while after a few tries, that was good enough.
She said knowing your whole fate could actually be bad for you, so fortunes were made so that not all of them come true.
But of course some of them do come true, so she wanted to believe the results as much as she could, and tell everyone about them on top of that.
What a personality, huh?{p}

But, well, she was really pretty.
So she was pretty popular with the boys.
When it came from Hirai, you could kind of forgive the lies, I guess.
There was something about Hirai you just couldn't hate.
She wasn't cheeky, see.
Even when she lied, if someone called her on it later, she'd apologize right away.
"I'm sorry," she'd say.
And when she looked at you with those beautiful, teary eyes, people said they somehow just couldn't stay mad.
People like that sure have it easy, huh?
But you know, there was also this rumor.{p}

Hirai's older brother had a scar on his hand that looked like it came from a knife cut.
The story was that he got it in a fight with his sister.
It's just a rumor, of course.
I don't know the details, though.{p}

So, {a}.
Earlier I said Hirai really wanted to get married, right?
But how should I put it...
It seems she didn't seriously want to be a housewife.
She wasn't the type to face reality much.
Like, her brother's wonderful, so she'll follow after him; she's a girl, so marriage is her dream; that kind of thing.
Simple-minded, you could say.
Basically, she was still a child.
So everyone used to say,
could she ever really get married?
And then...{p}

One day, her fortune said she would meet her destined someone in the near future.
What do you think she did?
Of course, she believed it and blabbed it to all sorts of people.
And then...
This time, it actually came true.
She met him.
Her ideal partner.{p}

It was the day of the school festival.
A third-year boy came into the cooking club's classroom, where she was working the reception desk.
He asked her two or three questions about the club's event.
His name was Suzuki.
Hirai couldn't stop thinking about him.
They say Suzuki looked a little like her brother, somehow.
During the school festival, every classroom has a notebook set out, right?
And visitors write their names in it.
Hirai copied down Suzuki's name and class from that notebook.{p}

And she started watching him from afar.
Suzuki was on the soccer team.
It seems Hirai often went to watch him practice.
He was cool, dependable, smart, and had a great personality...
So apparently Hirai fell for him right away.
Kind of a funny story, isn't it?
But I think that kind of love comes mostly from a girl's own assumptions.
A misunderstanding, you might call it?
Just because a guy's a little good-looking and confident, she goes, "He's so wonderful, he seems smart too, and his personality's A-OK..." and turns him into someone to idolize more and more.
And Hirai, well...{p}

Since her fortune about meeting Suzuki had come true, next she decided to read their compatibility.
The result was...
A-OK.
The two of them came out as a pretty good match.
So you can guess what she did, right?
She blabbed it to everyone.
That she and he were going to work out.{p}

Eventually, the story reached Suzuki's ears too.
He knew she'd been coming to watch the soccer team practice, but...
the only time he'd ever talked to her was briefly at the school festival.
And yet there was a rumor going around that the two of them were about to become a couple.
And they said it was Hirai who'd spread that rumor.{p}

...Suzuki went to see Hirai.
To talk to her.{p}So what do you think he said?
If you like me, let's go out
Stop spreading weird rumors

Suzuki said this to her.
"There seem to be rumors about you and me going around everywhere.
How serious are you about that?
If it's okay with you...
I'm thinking I'd like to go out with you."
She happily told him how she felt.
That she liked him.
And that it was fate, just as her fortune had shown.
...Hey, {a}.{p}What do you think Suzuki said then?
I feel like it's fate too
You're kind of weird

"Yeah.
I feel like it's fate too."
That's what he said.
A pretty girl he'd met at the school festival.
A girl who was always watching soccer practice.
He'd had his eye on Hirai too, after all.
If this was fate, he thought, he'd gladly accept it.{p}

The two of them started going out.
At first, it seems they were having fun.
She often told her friends this, apparently.
That she loved Suzuki.
That she wanted to marry him.
But...{p}

Whenever Suzuki said he was going to a game, she'd read the outcome.
If the result was bad, she'd beg him not to go to the game.
"Because there's definitely going to be an accident."
That's what she'd say.
Sure, in a soccer game you might get hurt...
But the way she worried was a little abnormal.
And Hirai's fortunes almost never came true, you know.
Her fortune about meeting Suzuki coming true was practically a miracle.
Suzuki started getting irritated.
It wasn't just the games; she was constantly doing readings and jerking him around.{p}
So one day after school, Suzuki had a talk with her.{p}What do you think he said?
Fix your personality
Let's break up

Suzuki told her to fix her personality.
Then she burst into tears.
"Suzuki, are you going to say that too?
The same thing my big brother said...?"
And with that, she sank down onto the hallway floor.
Suzuki frowned and looked down at her.
With a really disgusted look on his face.
She was hurt when she saw that.
And she said this.
"It's just like with my big brother.
Suzuki, you have the same eyes as my big brother..."{p}

"Aaaaagh☆"
He clutched his neck and groaned.
"I'm sorry, Suzuki.
I'm sorry...
But I can't hold on to your heart unless I do this.
Yes, my fortune said so.
If you want to keep the heart of the one you love, do whatever it takes.
Even if you have to use a blade.
It was like that with my big brother too.
My brother said he'd gotten a girlfriend.
But when I stabbed him with a box cutter, he broke up with her.
It went just like the fortune said.
But my brother's so mean.
He told me to fix my personality.
He told me to stop telling fortunes.
There's no way I could do that.
I love fortune-telling.
So, so..."{p}

Suzuki collapsed in the hallway, his hand groping at the air again and again as if begging for help.
But no one came to help him.
Everyone had already gone home.
Hirai gazed at him with her big round eyes, took her tarot cards out of her uniform pocket, and said this.{p}

"Suzuki, I'm sorry☆
I'll do a reading for you right now.
What do I do, I...
I only wanted to keep you with me.
But...
Oh, no.
The cards fell!{p}

Oh, it's Death.
This is the card of death.
Suzuki, are you going to die?
What do I do?
I wanted to marry you.
But if this is fate...
I'm sure nothing can be done about it..."
Muttering to herself, Hirai walked off down the hallway.
At the feet of the fallen Suzuki lay a single Death card...
...{p}

Afterward, Suzuki was saved by a teacher who happened to come by.
He got first aid right away and pulled through, I heard.
But because of this incident, she transferred to another school.
And before she left, she left behind one last fortune, they say.
"Someday, I'll come back to this school again."
Like that...
...
I wonder if it's true.
It's her fortune, so I don't think you can count on it, but...
Right, {a}?
You can't count on it, can you?
...That's the end of my story.
But they still haven't come, have they?
The seventh one.
Well, what should we do...?{p}

Suzuki laid into Hirai.
He told her to stop spreading weird rumors.
He was really popular.
So he often ran into girls like that, girls who made no sense.
That's why he chewed Hirai out, sounding kind of fed up.
If she'd only been watching soccer practice, maybe someday he would have said something kind to her.
But Suzuki ended up thinking he didn't want to go anywhere near a girl like her.{p}

Hirai was heartbroken.
Her fortune had been wrong, after all.
So she went right back to clinging to her big brother.
From the next day on, she talked about nothing but her brother.{p}

Her brother was the best after all, she said.
She didn't want anyone else.
The fortune that said her destined someone would appear had been wrong.
And then, one day...{p}

She came to school with a scar on her hand.
In exactly the same spot as her brother's scar.
Where do you think that spot was?
...Her wrist.
The place you cut when you kill yourself.
Everyone was shocked and rushed over to her.
To try to comfort her.
And then...{p}

She suddenly vanished, just like that.
...
...She had killed herself.
That's right. At that point, she was already no longer of this world.{p}

Before what happened with Suzuki, Hirai had told a fortune about her relationship with her brother.
And this is what came out, apparently.
If the two of them never parted, one of them would die...
Of course, she believed it.
So she tried to separate herself from her brother.
Believing the fortune that said she'd meet someone more wonderful than him.
But Suzuki turned her down.
So she thought it over.
Should she wait and see until either her brother or she died?
Or end one of their lives, so that only one of them would be saved...
The scar on her brother's wrist was there because she'd been agonizing over that, they say.
It seems her brother told Hirai this.
If you die for a reason like that, I'll follow you.
And then he cut his wrist to show her.
He seems to have figured that would keep Hirai from doing something rash like killing herself.
After that, Suzuki came along, and her brother seemed relieved, but...
Hirai got turned down.
She decided there was nothing left but for her to die.
The sadness of a broken heart played a part too.
And so she cut her wrist.{p}

...Hey, {a}.
Don't you think fortune-telling is scary?
Whether it'll really come true.
Or whether it won't.
You can't know that until you go through it yourself.
And besides...
There might be people who change their fate to fit a fortune after they've had it told, right?
I don't think Hirai died because of fate, though.
What do you think, {a}...?
...{p}

That's the end of my story.
But...
All six of us have told our stories now.
And the seventh one still isn't here.
What do you want to do?
{a}...?{p}

"What are you talking about?
...You're kind of weird."
Suzuki frowned.
He must have thought that she might have a pretty face, but her personality was scary.
He was popular, so he knew very well what happened when you got mixed up with a girl like that.
So he flatly turned her down.{p}

"Sorry.
I hate to say it, but I'll have to pass on going out with a girl like you."
And then he just walked off, apparently.
Hirai was left all alone, crying, they say.
Her fortune had been wrong this time too.{p}
